title: The aim
text: Build monsters out of cards, then set armies of babies on everyone's monsters at once. Monsters that are strong enough eat the babies, and eaten babies are points. Most points when the deck runs out wins.

title: Building a monster
text:
A monster starts with a head. Bodies, arms, legs and tools are stitched on where the stitches on the cards line up. Every part adds to its strength, shown on the cards.

Each head belongs to land, sea or sky, and so does the monster built on it.

title: The babies
text: Baby cards are never kept in your hand. When you draw one it goes face down in the middle, in the army of its kind: land, sea or sky. The armies grow quietly while you build.

title: Provoking
text:
On your turn you may provoke one baby army instead of doing anything else. It attacks every monster of its kind on the table, all players at once.

Add up the babies. The player with the strongest monster of that kind, if it beats the babies' total, eats the lot and keeps them as points. Every monster of that kind is then discarded, win or lose.

title: What I do not carry
text: How many actions a turn allows depends on the number of players, and the special cards explain themselves. Your rule sheet has both. I will keep the turn order and count the babies each of you has eaten.
